#5298. 17 Years Ago, Satoshi Nakamoto Opens His BitcoinTalk Account: What Happened Next

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

The network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed users on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

In 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and announced their farewell.

The 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an issue we haven't solved 17 years later.

2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of new technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

However, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, issues with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

In 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

The next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

Options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI

This suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

According to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

At the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history says more than its current price action does.

XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

In the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. On Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

According to the entry, the company claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator said.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure users with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

On the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

On Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he said.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

#5295. Bitcoin Bounces From $62K: Is Gold and Silver’s 14% Crash Sending Money Into Crypto?

BTC bounced from $62K as silver fell 14% since Nov 9. What does fund trading reveal, and is there really a shift from metals into Bitcoin?

In today’s Bitcoin news, on November 19, silver and gold are extending their sell-off, but Bitcoin is holding its ground near $63,800. BTC has bounced off the $62,000 level for the second time in four days, raising the question of whether crypto’s sell-off is finally losing steam and investors are starting to move money back into digital assets.

Silver futures closed Wednesday at $45 an ounce, down 4.8% on the day and 14% since November 9, while gold fell another 3.2%.

JUST IN: $1,400,000,000,000 wiped out from Gold and Silver in the past 24 hours. pic.twitter.com/NwLlK9b1iv

— Whale Insider (@WhaleInsider) November 19, 2026

For traders following Bitcoin news, the obvious explanation is that money is moving out of metals and into crypto. We tested that by comparing how much money changes hands each day in the three largest US funds for silver, gold, and Bitcoin. If investors were switching, Bitcoin’s slice of that trading would grow.

Well, for now it hasn’t: Bitcoin took 30% of the money traded over the past five trading days, about the same as the 31% it took over the 20 days before.

Bitcoin’s bounce also came with less trading than the sell-off before it, a sign that buyers are still cautious.

So is this the start of a shift from metals to crypto, or just a pause in the selling?

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) give a clean view of where US money goes, because they trade side by side on the same exchanges. We took the three biggest: the iShares Silver Trust (SLV), SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), and BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT). For each, we multiplied the closing price by the shares traded to get the dollars that changed hands each day.

So the money leaving silver and gold isn’t showing up in Bitcoin funds, at least not yet. It looks more like a broad sell-off in both, with metals now taking the heavier hit.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Binance’s BTCUSDT pair tells the same Bitcoin news story from the crypto side. During the drop from November 13 to 15, it traded an average of $2.0 billion a day. In the three days since, as Bitcoin held above $62,000, the average fell to $1.5 billion.

Lighter trading on a bounce means fewer buyers are stepping in. Sellers have slowed down, but buyers haven’t rushed back.

Bitcoin’s spot ETFs, which hold the coin itself, show a similar picture. IBIT took in $76.5 million on November 16, its first inflow after 11 days of outflows. That’s a start, but one day of buying after two weeks of selling.

What drives both markets is the same: the US Federal Reserve. Traders expect another rate hike in December, and higher rates hurt assets that pay no interest, from silver to Bitcoin. Until that changes, a rotation from one to the other has little to feed on.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Return After Seven-Day Losing Streak as IBIT Adds $76.5M: Is the Sell-Off Finally Over?

On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $63,713. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,245, and its 200-day EMA at $75,624.

The Bitcoin news to watch is volume. A move above $65,500 with trading back near $2 billion a day would be a start. If IBIT’s share of fund trading also climbs above a third, money is actually moving from metals to crypto.

#5294. Arthur Hayes Says Anthropic IPO Could Determine Bitcoin’s Next Move

Maelstrom CEO Arthur Hayes projected that the outcome of Anthropic’s IPO could impact digital assets above the current baseline. This follows a string of analysts citing fund rotation as a reason for capital flight over the last three months.

The crypto executive hinted that the much-anticipated IPO’s performance would be felt throughout the sector. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has dominated financial markets, raising expectations for the company’s stock price and related projects.

According to Hayes, a weak IPO would negatively impact digital assets and drag Bitcoin’s price lower. The top crypto dipped into the red zone, plunging trader sentiment after its price hit a new three-month low.

Conversely, a strong IPO would be bullish for crypto assets, especially Bitcoin, by boosting market confidence. Hayes’ view may stem from the year-long correlation between Bitcoin and the United States stock market, though risks remain.

“If Anthropic struggles or treads water, then it’s trouble for the entire market… I want to see Anthropic IPO perform, but what matters is the sentiment around AI, can Anthropic pull off a successful IPO. This is the bellwether for the whole story… Massive pop off the IPO, it’s game back on, it’s long everything, risk on.”

For bears, although institutional investors going bullish on tech stocks results in crypto’s win, this year has been different. Capital rotation to tech stocks occasioned mass crypto liquidations. Basically, investors dumped assets and jumped on the AI bandwagon, creating different views on the IPO’s impact.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao cited talks around Anthropic IPO as a factor behind Bitcoin’s decline. The top crypto trades under $62,000, making a consistent decline amid a slew of macro and industry factors.

Strive CEO Matt Cole explained that Bitcoin fell 19% during the SpaceX IPO and is down 18% heading into the second-largest IPO. “What happened after the SpaceX IPO is the notable part. Bitcoin bottomed 18 days after the listing, then recovered all the way. By Day 100, it was above where it started.”

Crypto users expect a slow turnaround because institutional sentiment needed for a rebound is at sharp lows due to infamous hacks and tighter regulations.

Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that users will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

Binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Users are strongly advised to update and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

In related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in users’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) held no shares of the Teucrium 2x Long Daily XRP ETF at the end of the second quarter, according to an amended Form 13F that the bank filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Nov. 18, 2026. The Teucrium fund gives investors double leveraged exposure to XRP.

In the first quarter of 2026, RBC reported buying shares of the spot Bitwise XRP ETF for about $30,000. XRP was trading at $0.99 on Thursday.

The latest wave of 13F filings came out in November and covers the third quarter through Sept. 30. Goldman Sachs held about $144 million in XRP ETFs at the end of the third quarter, up from about $87 million at the end of the second quarter, according to its filing. The bank held shares of five spot funds from Franklin Templeton, Bitwise, Canary, Grayscale and 21Shares, and its crypto portfolio was worth $2.64 billion.

Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed XRP fund holdings of $27.21 million. The bank held 712,319 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF, worth about $20.52 million, and it also opened a new position of 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF, worth about $6.7 million. Besides, trading firm Jane Street reported about $23.5 million in XRP funds.

UBS and Morgan Stanley disclosed XRP fund holdings of $1.91 million and $116,000, respectively. Bank of America held 13,260 shares of the futures-based Volatility Shares XRP ETF, worth about $106,600.

Wells Fargo held about $11,000 in the Bitwise fund, and JPMorgan Chase held 539 shares of the same fund, worth about $9,000. National Bank of Canada held 330 shares of the Bitwise fund, worth about $5,500, and Bank of Montreal held REX-Osprey and ProShares Ultra XRP shares worth $4,300.

U.S. spot XRP ETFs held $1.08 billion in total assets as of Nov. 17, according to SoSoValue.

Form 13F filings only capture long positions in US-listed securities on a specific date. They don't show shorts, derivative hedges, intra-quarter trading or assets held outside the United States.

#5287. XRP Outperforms Solana and Dogecoin in Japan

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the company highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This shows that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are currently trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data showed Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

DacityCoin (DCTY) hit an $18 million market cap, the day Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI. But what is DacityCoin? Traders were racing to find GTA 6 meme coins before the game had even finished downloading.

DacityCoin’s fomo doubled PumpSwap’s daily volume on Wednesday, yet the exchange was busier than it was on 12 days since October 1. Dogecoin, Pepe and Bonk barely blinked, and Pump.fun’s own token, PUMP, is sitting near a one-month low.

So is this the spark for a new run in meme coins, or just a fun one-day side quest?

DacityCoin started as a background joke. In Rockstar’s launch trailer, the name is painted on a stunt plane. Then this week, gameplay footage from Brazilian streamer Combo Infinito showed an in-game phone app listing “DacityCoin (DCTY)”, complete with buy and sell buttons.

Crypto traders did what crypto traders do: within hours, the Solana token with the same ticker went vertical.

Before the footage, DCTY had never been worth more than about $54,000. Here’s what its main pool on DEX Screener shows now:

A separate Pump.fun token called “Dacity Coin” hit a $10.8 million market value on Wednesday, then slid to about $800,000. Exchange Bitrue joined in as well, listing DacityCoin futures with up to 10x leverage on Wednesday.

If a fresh meme coin season were kicking off, Pump.fun is where you’d see it first, since that’s where most new Solana tokens of this kind are born. So we pulled PumpSwap’s daily trading from DefiLlama, which tracks exchange data across blockchains.

Outside the GTA hype, the bigger meme coins are having a rough year. All eight large meme coins we tracked on Binance are down for 2026, by a median of 54%, while Bitcoin is down 28%. The past week stung too, with drops between 11% and 23%:

The worst day was November 14, when PUMP dropped 15%. Token trackers list a scheduled release of locked PUMP tokens in mid-November, though they don’t agree on the exact date. So far, buybacks of under $1 million a day haven’t been enough to soak up that selling.

GTA 6 meme coins are hot now, but the thing to watch is breadth, meaning how many coins move together. If PumpSwap volume stays above $300 million a day after launch week and Dogecoin or Pepe join in, DacityCoin could be the start of something bigger.

If DCTY fades and volume slips back to $150 million, it’ll go down as a fun launch-day story and not much more.

#5284. What’s Coming for Solana in 2027? Upgrade Planned Across Four Key Areas

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

The Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

After Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

According to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

“So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more quickly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

“Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

Watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”

#5281. XRP and Solana ETF Plans Abruptly Scrapped After Yearlong Wait

Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated plans to launch two new XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

As per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn plans to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

Interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its plans to launch these two ETFs.

Roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

Unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

Notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

The ETF industry is entering a new phase of competition. Once dominated by low-cost index funds, the market is expanding into active management, cryptocurrency exposure, derivatives-based strategies and specialized investment themes. The shift is changing how asset managers develop products and compete for investor capital. Global ETF assets reached $22.83 trillion in September 2026, while U.S.-listed funds attracted another $204.2 billion in October. Yet the more important change is happening in capital allocation: investors are increasingly using ETFs to access strategies that extend well beyond traditional market indexes.

This report examines the key trends reshaping the ETF market, the rise of new investment products, and how these developments could redefine asset management.

The global ETF market added more than $4 trillion in assets during the first nine months of 2026, supported by investor inflows and gains across financial markets. According to data, global ETF assets increased from $18.69 trillion at the end of 2025 to $22.83 trillion by September 30, 2026. Net inflows contributed $2.25 trillion, while market appreciation added another $1.89 trillion.

More significantly, nine-month inflows had already exceeded the previous full-year record of $2.09 trillion set in 2025. Equity ETFs remained the industry’s largest segment, with $17.74 trillion in assets, followed by bond ETFs at $3.57 trillion. Alternative ETFs held $772.1 billion, while commodity ETFs accounted for $471.7 billion.

Active management is emerging as one of the ETF industry’s fastest-growing segments. The appeal is straightforward: investors can access portfolio managers’ security selection and allocation decisions through an exchange-traded structure. The latest inflow figures suggest that demand is expanding faster than the segment’s existing asset share.

Active ETFs attracted $675.2 billion in net inflows during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $1.58 trillion for passive products. That gave active funds nearly 30% of total ETF inflows, despite representing just 12.81% of industry assets.

The gap between asset share and inflow share is significant. Active ETFs are attracting a larger proportion of new money than their current market presence would suggest. Product launches reinforce that shift. Of the 89 U.S. ETFs launched in October, 65% were actively managed, according to FactSet. Equity strategies accounted for approximately half of new launches.

Cryptocurrency ETFs have created a new distribution channel between digital assets and traditional financial markets. Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum products allow investors to gain exposure through conventional brokerage accounts rather than directly managing wallets, private keys or exchange accounts. This has made digital assets more accessible to investors who prefer established investment platforms and fund structures.

The development also brings traditional asset managers into direct competition for crypto allocations. Firms such as BlackRock and Fidelity can distribute digital asset products through established investment networks, while specialist providers compete through product design, fees and market positioning.

Crypto ETFs remain exposed to price volatility, custody arrangements, liquidity conditions and regulatory uncertainty. The wider significance is that digital assets are becoming part of the ETF product landscape rather than remaining confined to dedicated cryptocurrency exchanges.

Options-based ETFs are expanding the range of outcomes investors can pursue through exchange-traded products. Covered-call funds, buffer ETFs and defined-outcome strategies are increasingly being used to target income, manage downside exposure or modify participation in market gains.

The growth of ETF-linked derivatives trading provides a measure of the activity surrounding these products. Cboe reported that ETF options averaged 28.3 million contracts per day in the third quarter of 2026, up 1% from the previous quarter. Single-stock options averaged 32.7 million contracts, while index options recorded 6.1 million.

The activity highlights ETFs’ growing role in the derivatives market. It also provides an important foundation for products built around option premiums and defined investment outcomes.

Asset managers are increasingly using thematic ETFs to package exposure to industries expected to benefit from long-term economic and technological changes.

Artificial intelligence, semiconductor manufacturing, cybersecurity, defense, nuclear energy and critical minerals are among the themes attracting investment interest. These products allow investors to access groups of companies linked to a particular industry without selecting individual stocks.

The scale of the broader U.S. ETF market illustrates the opportunity. U.S. ETF assets increased from $12.63 trillion in September 2025 to $16.15 trillion in September 2026, while the number of funds expanded from 4,181 to 5,368, according to the Investment Company Institute.

The ETF expansion is not being driven exclusively by new investment products. Traditional asset managers are also reconsidering how existing strategies are packaged and distributed.

Mutual fund-to-ETF conversions offer a route to bring established portfolios into an exchange-traded structure. For eligible U.S. funds, the structure can provide potential tax advantages, intraday trading and access to brokerage distribution networks. The shift is particularly relevant for active managers. Instead of building a new strategy from the ground up, firms can consider offering existing investment approaches through ETFs.

October’s launch activity illustrates the direction of product development: 65% of the 89 new U.S. ETFs launched that month were actively managed. FactSet also reported that equity strategies represented approximately half of those launches.

The growing complexity of ETF strategies is bringing regulatory oversight into sharper focus. On June 30, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission issued a request for public comment on ETFs seeking exposure to innovative asset classes or using novel investment strategies. The consultation examined how regulators could accommodate product innovation while maintaining investor protection and orderly markets.

The SEC raised questions around the regulatory status of certain novel ETFs, their oversight and the registration process. The public comment deadline was August 31, 2026.

The SEC has not finalized a new rule through this request. However, its review could influence how future products are structured and evaluated. For asset managers, regulatory clarity will be an important factor in determining how quickly new investment strategies can reach the market.

The ETF industry is moving beyond its traditional role as a low-cost vehicle for index investing. Active products are attracting a larger share of new capital, crypto funds are extending access to digital assets, and options-based strategies are giving investors more targeted ways to manage portfolios.

Yet traditional equity and bond funds continue to dominate industry assets. The next phase of growth will depend on whether specialized products can maintain investor demand while delivering clear investment value.

#5271. Uhm, Netflix, What Is This? CZ Slams The Altruists for Making Him the Villain Behind FTX’s Collapse

The Altruists by Netflix makes CZ the villain of FTX’s fall. Our FTT data shows the crash came after FTX asked Binance for help.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, known as CZ, has hit back at The Altruists Netflix series about the fall of FTX, which premiered on November 19. The show has found a villain for the story, and it is not the man serving 25 years in prison for it.

The Altruists Netflix release is a scripted drama, not a documentary, which may explain a few things. Its eight episodes follow Sam Bankman-Fried, played by Anthony Boyle, and his former girlfriend Caroline Ellison. Terry Chen plays CZ, cast as the rival who brought Bankman-Fried down.

There are forces spreading negative narratives, with massive amounts of funding behind it. https://t.co/Ymy4sA0cJd

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) November 20, 2026

The real story is hardly a mystery. A US jury convicted Bankman-Fried of fraud after a month-long trial, and a judge sentenced him to 25 years in prison. Three years on, Netflix has somehow reopened the question of who is to blame. So did CZ and Binance really sink FTX, as the show suggests?

We went back to the token prices from the week FTX fell to check.

The series, co-created by Graham Moore and Jacqueline Hoyt, is built around Bankman-Fried’s relationship with Ellison, who ran Alameda Research, FTX’s sister trading firm. Netflix’s own page for the show sums it up in one line: “Young, idealistic and suddenly worth billions, they tried to do good—but unleashed the worst in each other.”

Zhao is a supporting character, but a central one in the plot. The show has him setting a trap that pushes Bankman-Fried into front-running, which means trading ahead of customers’ orders to profit from them. Some viewers also read it as pressure on FTX to hand over trading data.

Critics have attacked the show on other points too. Constance Wang, FTX’s former chief operating officer, who is a character in the series, criticized its inaccuracies and its framing as a love story. Other critics say the focus on the couple’s romance downplays Bankman-Fried’s own responsibility for the fraud.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Binance Listings

CZ did not write a long rebuttal. On the morning of November 20, he shared a Forbes commentary on X. The piece said The Altruists Netflix storyline turns him into a “crypto villain” and invents the front-running trap, and that there is no public evidence Zhao ever did such a thing.

He also posted a comparison image from March. In his words, it “already said it all.” Later that day he went further, saying that forces backed by huge financial support are spreading negative stories about him. He did not say who.

Yi He, Binance’s co-founder, was blunter. In a post in Chinese, she called the show’s characters thin and clichéd. “If you’re the protagonist, even your crimes are someone else’s fault,” she wrote. She compared it unfavourably with Hongguo, a Chinese short-drama app, and added: “Netflix might as well cancel it outright.”

Netflix and the showrunners have not responded publicly.

EXPLORE: BNB Crypto Drops 8.7% in an Hour as Binance Loses $6.36 Billion to Hackers, and Futures Traders Turn Short: Can BNB Hold Its 200-Day Average?

The real Binance did play a part in the final week. Here is the order of events in November 2022:

To see which of these moments broke FTX, we tracked FTT’s hourly price on Binance through that week.

Zhao’s post alone did not sink the token. FTT traded at $24.34 in the hour he posted it. Thirty-three hours later, at midnight UTC on November 8, it was still at $22.08, only 9% lower. Ellison had publicly offered to buy Binance’s FTT at $22, and the price held close to that.

The real crash came on November 8. FTT closed the hour of the deal announcement at $17.93, then hit $2.51 three hours later, a fall of 86%. That is when a run became a collapse: the rescue deal told the market that FTX could not pay its customers on its own.

Today FTT trades at about $0.17, down 99.3% from the hour of Zhao’s post.

A run like this only kills an exchange that does not hold its customers’ money. FTX did not. About $8 billion in customer deposits was missing, used to cover Alameda’s trading losses and spending.

At the 2023 trial, Ellison testified that Alameda had been taking FTX customer money for years, on Bankman-Fried’s instructions. The jury convicted him on all seven counts. The US Attorney’s Office in Manhattan announced in March 2024 that he had been sentenced to 25 years and ordered to forfeit about $11 billion. Ellison received two years.

Zhao has a criminal record of his own, from a separate case. He pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to run an effective anti-money-laundering program at Binance and served four months in prison. Binance agreed to pay more than $4 billion, and President Trump pardoned him in October 2025.

Sam Bankman-Fried may be the UNLUCKIEST investor in history.

If FTX hadn’t SOLD its investments after the collapse, it would still hold:

Anthropic: $34.7 billion (69x)Robinhood: $4.3 billion (7x)Solana: $2.9 billion (1.1x)Cursor: $1.8 billion (9,000x)Sui: $600 million (6x)… pic.twitter.com/GdHj3Lldaw

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) November 16, 2026

The FTX estate has also gone after Binance. In November 2024 it sued Binance and Zhao for about $1.76 billion, saying the 2021 buyback of Binance’s FTX stake was paid with customer money. It also claimed his November 2022 posts helped set off the run. Binance has called the claims meritless.

So The Altruists Netflix version is right that Zhao’s post lit the fuse. It leaves out that the hole was there long before he posted, and FTT’s price only collapsed once FTX had to ask for a rescue.

Anthropic has set a new historic precedent, having successfully raised about $81 billion in its initial public offering (IPO). This is the biggest IPO ever.

The artificial intelligence company sold 980 million shares at $83 per share, significantly higher than its previously announced price range of $70 to $78.

This brought Anthropic's initial valuation to about $1.5 trillion, making the company one of the most valuable publicly listed firms in the world right from the get-go.

But as Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq exchange, the ANT ticker saw massive volatility.

The listing of Anthropic shares is just one of Coinbase's moves to enter traditional financial markets.

#5268. Bitcoin miner fees hit a 15-year low – Why profit margins are shrinking

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

As 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure. This, in turn has resulted in miners increasingly selling their Bitcoin reserves instead of holding them for long-term appreciation.

According to Glassnode’s recent update, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.

This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.

At the same time, there is also a decline in transaction fee revenue. With 11 months into 2026, Bitcoin miners earned just 912 BTC in transaction fees, the lowest annual total since at least 2011. This is a huge drop compared to 1,720 BTC in 2025 and 15,178 BTC in 2024.

In other words, transaction fees accounted for only 0.63% of total miner revenue in 2026, down from 1% in 2025 and 6.5% in 2023. This is enough proof that demand for Bitcoin block space has weakened, reducing the contribution of this revenue source.

Remarking on the same, CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock said,

Like with any commodity production business, it should get harder and thinner margin over time because the lowest cost operators should be the most successful and durable.

In other words, Sudock believes Bitcoin mining will become increasingly competitive over the next decade, with shrinking profit margins favoring operators with the lowest production and electricity costs.

He expects the global hashrate to continue growing, but at a slower pace than in the previous ten years, as mining hardware becomes more efficient and large publicly listed miners explore AI data centers.

He also argued that Bitcoin mining will not depend solely on large public companies, as smaller businesses and privately held miners can operate profitably.

At the same time, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju noted that Bitcoin’s average mining cost reached approximately $62,862 in Q3 2026, based on Marathon Digital’s filings. With BTC trading near this level, miners are facing shrinking profit margins and could face potential losses if prices fall further.

However, the relatively high hashrate suggests miners remain committed to the network despite growing profitability concerns.

This comes as Bitcoin miners are shifting their focus towards AI and high-performance computing (HPC), as investors increasingly value their power infrastructure and data centers.

Companies such as Core Scientific, IREN, and TeraWulf are generating significant revenue from AI infrastructure and HPC services, in some cases surpassing their Bitcoin mining income.

However, the Miner Outflow chart suggests that compared with the rest of the year, November outflows are calm.

At the same time, the Miner Reserve chart was at about 1.1925 million BTC at press time. In fact, through October and into November, it moved in a narrow band, roughly between 1.192 million and 1.1926 million.

All in all, miners are roughly holding steady, with small accumulation or lower net selling.

#5266. Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, new research reveals.

A new report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical users into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue users, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Public GitHub activity shows a clear change in focus. New repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

Among AI users, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot launches rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:

In Bitrue’s survey of users who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents said they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

Among non-users, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot said they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

Users who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:

AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

The numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

#5262. Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch

Grayscale’s latest report highlights a hidden risk that still catches market-timing investors off guard.

New research from Grayscale shows Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.

The catch? Bitcoin’s calmer day-to-day trading hides a massive trap for anyone trying to time dips: almost all of its multi-year gains still come from just a handful of explosive trading days.

In its report, “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Cryptocurrency Risks,” US digital asset manager Grayscale says Bitcoin’s long-term performance is heavily influenced by a handful of trading days. Its returns have “fat tails,” meaning sharp gains and losses occur more frequently than in traditional stocks.

Over the past three years, Bitcoin delivered an annualized return of roughly 60%. Excluding its 10 best days would have cut that figure to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would have raised it to 197%.

The report also notes that Bitcoin has historically rebounded sharply after major declines. Since 2011, it has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50%, although Grayscale says these declines are not unusually severe compared with stocks and bonds when adjusted for volatility.

Grayscale also sees Bitcoin as a potential portfolio diversifier because it is less exposed to traditional market factors.

The company points out that Bitcoin has historically recovered sharply after significant declines. Since 2011, Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns of more than 50% from previous highs.

The report cites Bitcoin’s inclusion in J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions as a milestone.

Grayscale describes JPMorgan as a $5 trillion investment manager that now examines Bitcoin alongside established asset classes.

The banks’ 10-year base case for Bitcoin projects a 10% compound annualized return for Bitcoin over the next decade, the highest among the asset classes covered. The forecast also assumes 55% annualized volatility and a 33% correlation with US large-cap stocks, the number below international equities, corporate bonds and hedge funds.

In Bitcoin’s early years, volatility routinely exceeded 100% and at times approached 200%, with a market cap in the single-digit billions.

Grayscale ties the decline to roughly 43% to larger market value and liquidity, greater institutional participation, Bitcoin exchange-traded products and regulatory clarity.

In historical tests, modest Bitcoin allocations raised annualized return and Sharpe ratio in a representative institutional portfolio.

Over three years, Bitcoin explained about half of return variation across FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over the past two years, while Bitcoin led none.

JPMorgan’s decision to include Bitcoin in its long-term forecasts, along with declining volatility, could shape how institutions approach crypto investments. At the same time, Grayscale’s data shows how much Bitcoin’s long-term performance depends on a small number of trading days, highlighting the risks of trying to time the market.

Bitcoin Bitcoin Every bull market phase in BTC's history has ended with at least a 75% correction of the previous parabolic bull trend. Could this be what's happening in Bitcoin? https://t.co/PVXJpetSyO

Brandt's latest doomsday prediction comes at a time when Bitcoin is still trying to recover from its biggest sell-off to date, which has wiped out close to half of its market value from its October 2025 peak.

Italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a new disclosure. This follows capital rotation out of Bitcoin products by a slew of traditional firms amid dwindling market sentiment.

The bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways. In June, total assets were worth $90 million as it looked to diversify and grow holdings systematically.

Bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets. At the end of Q2, BTC holdings stood at $69.32 million but dropped slightly to above $61 million last quarter. The firm’s Ethereum exposure also dropped to $5 million.

However, Solana and XRP products filled the vacuum, highlighting institutional appetite for these assets. At the time of writing, the bank’s spot Solana ETF exposure is at $14.1 million after its investment in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF ballooned from seven shares to 875,407 shares.

Intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The company’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

More broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

Historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

The former have the potential to record spikes within the red wave, like in 2022 before the approval of spot ETF products in the United States. These products opened up digital assets to a new stash of traditional capital.

Intesa and other banks have since increased their crypto exposure, driven by the need to diversify assets and a broader adoption spree. S&P Global Ratings assigned a score of 5 to Tether’s USDT, the weakest in its five-point stablecoin stability scale. What’s more surprising here is the fact that the assessment, which was published on the 18th of November, 2026, has remained unchanged since November 2025.

This was mainly because there was a growing proportion of higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves. According to S&P Global, these assets accounted for 28% of circulating USDT as of the 30th of September 2026, compared with 24% in 2025.

Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.

That said, Tether’s reserve composition has also shifted over the past year, with gold holdings rising from $12.9 billion in September 2025 to $19 billion in September 2026. Meanwhile, the company also added $4.2 billion in publicly traded equities, while its Bitcoin holdings declined from $9.9 billion to $8.4 billion.

Yet, despite the growing exposure to riskier assets, Tether reported $191.45 billion in reserves against $183.50 billion in liabilities as of the 30th of September. This in turn left a reserve buffer of approximately $7.95 billion and a collateralization ratio of 104.3%, up from 103.9% in 2025.

Still, above all of this, USDT traded close to its $1 peg over the past year, while its market capitalization grew from $158 billion to approximately $184 billion between September 2025 and September 2026.

However, according to a recent AMBCrypto report, Tether’s market capitalization dropped by $6.6 billion over the course of sixty days, ending on the 7th of November.

Bitcoin (BTC) price continues to fall as the sell-off from the $86,000 - $87,000 region in October is gathering momentum. The sell-off has accelerated in recent days, and BTC price has slipped to roughly $61,900, moving closer to the next technical support level at $60,000.

The daily chart shows several concerning technical developments for Bitcoin. Shorter-term moving averages continue to fall below longer-term moving averages, forming a technical pattern commonly known as a death cross. The death cross has now formed twice with 100 and 200 EMAs, indicating a worsening technical setup for Bitcoin, commonly known as a double death cross.

Several key moving averages continue to cluster in the $75,000 - $76,000 region, adding resistance for Bitcoin price action.

Relative Strength Index (RSI) has started to move closer to the oversold region, indicating that momentum has started to slow for Bitcoin.

Taken together, this technical setup indicates that selling pressure for Bitcoin has been increasing on multiple time frames. We are monitoring $60,000 as a key support level. This level was also an area of interest for buyers during the June correction in Bitcoin.

Should BTC price continue to move lower and break out below $60,000, the next level of support to watch will be $58,000, followed by $56,000.

For Bitcoin price to reverse course and show signs of a meaningful short-term rebound, it will need to continue higher and break out above $64,000 - $65,000.

Breaking out above $68,000 would be a strong move that could help to stabilize Bitcoin in the short term. A positive move for Bitcoin would need to continue higher and reclaim several key moving averages. Until then, Bitcoin will continue to trade in a more bearish technical setup.

Bitcoin price action continues to move lower on the daily chart. All technical indicators on this chart continue to deteriorate, indicating that Bitcoin remains vulnerable to another leg lower before buyers can show signs of a robust short-term recovery.

#5252. Binance Hack-Linked Wallet Moves 34,279 ETH, but Investigators See No Confirmed Sale

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of inactivity. The ether was worth roughly $63 million at prices used in Tuesday’s reporting. That is a significant movement of suspected stolen funds, but a wallet transfer is not automatically a sale, a successful laundering step or proof that the recipient controls are independent of the sender. Investigators had not identified the new addresses as exchanges at the time of their initial reports.

Monitoring groups MistTrack and Solid Intel reported the transfers on November 17. MistTrack described three movements of approximately 12,000 ETH, 12,000 ETH and 10,279.66 ETH. The receiving wallets were newly created, and the monitored funds had not moved again when the analysts published their findings. Public transaction records make it possible to trace the amounts and destinations, but they do not disclose the human operator behind each address. The link to the earlier breach rests on investigators’ attribution of the sending wallet, not a label embedded in the blockchain itself.

The October attack involved vastly larger losses than Tuesday’s movement. US investigators attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking group, and authorities have announced substantial asset restraints and seizures. Blockchain intelligence firms have also tracked funds moved through different assets and protocols. These parallel developments should not be added together casually, because frozen, seized, recovered and still-controlled amounts describe different legal and operational states. The fresh ETH transfers are one piece of a complex post-incident trail rather than an update to the full net-loss number.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's custody and security precautions.

Crypto trading commentary sometimes treats any transfer from an exploit-linked wallet as preparation to dump tokens. That can happen, but the evidence here does not yet establish a market sale. Transfers may consolidate funds, redistribute control or precede another operation. Until an address is linked to a trading venue, bridge, mixer or other service, the immediate observable fact is the destination change. Even a later exchange deposit would need careful interpretation: deposits are not identical to executed sell orders. Reporting should preserve those steps rather than collapsing them into one dramatic conclusion.

Ethereum’s public ledger lets investigators monitor known addresses and alert service providers if assets reappear at identifiable points. Token issuers, exchanges and law enforcement may each have different powers depending on the assets and jurisdictions involved. Native ETH cannot simply be frozen by an issuer in the way some centrally administered tokens can. That difference complicates recovery when funds leave services that can intervene. The next useful evidence will be further movements, identification of services receiving the funds and official updates to the case.

Investigators can improve attribution confidence by comparing the sequence, amounts and transaction timing with addresses already associated with the incident. Yet public labels can be incomplete, and a newly created wallet may simply be another address controlled by the same actor. Readers should resist claims that funds have reached a criminal group, a particular country or a cash-out desk unless that identification is supported by additional evidence. Future investigative notices should specify their degree of confidence and distinguish observed transfers from hypotheses about their purpose.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet compromise.

The latest transfer warrants close monitoring, but it should not be reported as the disposal of $63 million in stolen ether without further proof. The distinction between observable transactions and inferred intent is especially important in a security incident of this scale.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk report of MistTrack and Solid Intel monitoring · MistTrack transfer report

Bitcoin’s [BTC] price slide is accelerating, with the king coin falling below $63,000 amid a new wave of ETF outflows and a broader rotation of capital into the AI sector.

The drop extends a brutal month that has seen roughly $2.58 billion flee U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs since the start of November.

On the 19th of November, Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of $306.50 million, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $209.5 million, roughly 87% of the day’s redemptions.

The price action followed the outflows, as Bitcoin traded near $63,071 at the time of writing, down nearly 3% on the day and hovering at its lowest levels since mid-August. Ethereum fared worse, though, dropping below $1,800 at press time.

Another massive factor behind Bitcoin’s fall was noted by the X account Why Markets Move. It stated that currently, investors are seeing more potential in the AI boom and the upcoming Anthropic IPO, compared to crypto.

For the uninitiated, Anthropic is currently targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its Nasdaq listing, with investors such as Nvidia and Microsoft. This is undoubtedly good news for AI, but not such much for digital assets.

Raj Kamal, founder and CEO of TransFi, told AMBCrypto how policy shifts and macro conditions can crush crypto sentiment. He said,

I think the market read the result as a short-term negative for crypto. #5250. Bitcoin missed AI stocks’ 85% rally but could still face the fallout if the boom unravels

Bitcoin fell on 77% of major Nasdaq down days since January 2024, a pattern drawing attention as the Fed examines risks from AI-related debt and financing.

DWF Labs reported on Nov. 19 that Bitcoin fell on 77% of US trading days when QQQ, an ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100, lost at least 1%.

The analysis covers the period from the start of US spot Bitcoin ETF trading on Jan. 11, 2024, through Nov. 13, 2026. DWF put Bitcoin’s average decline on large Nasdaq down days at about 2%.

In the Federal Reserve’s October meeting minutes, released Nov. 18, almost all participants discussed what could happen if returns on artificial intelligence investments disappointed. Most pointed to rapid growth in AI-related debt and the complex, opaque structures used to finance much of it.

From September 2025 through the end of the study’s data on Nov. 13, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained 85% while Bitcoin fell 39%, according to DWF Labs.

If an AI selloff spreads from chip stocks to the wider Nasdaq-100, Bitcoin’s record on those down days becomes more relevant than its trading during the chip rally.

At the Oct. 27-28 meeting, many participants discussed the potential consequences of AI-related assets losing value if investors became less confident about the returns.

A few noted that exposure was becoming concentrated among a small number of firms, raising questions about how the buildout was financed and what the projects themselves might earn.

Fed staff flagged two structures that could amplify losses if returns disappointed.

One was off-balance-sheet leases, which can leave firms committed to future payments that do not appear on their balance sheets. The other was circular financing among AI-related firms, which ties their funding to one another.

Investors who borrowed to buy assets might have to sell holdings to reduce their debt, while fund managers might also need to sell to meet withdrawals. In the most severe scenarios, sales by vehicles such as hedge funds, bond mutual funds and target-date funds could make it harder for markets to absorb trades.

Elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage were the biggest vulnerabilities in the staff assessment. Strong bank and household balance sheets offered a buffer against more severe outcomes, and several participants noted the staff’s finding that banks were well capitalized.

Some participants saw gaps in the picture, and several questioned whether supervisors had enough data on banks’ indirect exposure through nonbank institutions, such as credit lines to private credit funds.

The minutes describe a stress scenario in which an asset-price decline compounds through financing commitments, leverage and the need to raise cash.

The connection for Bitcoin investors would depend on whether those pressures move beyond AI-related firms and pull down the wider market.

DWF Labs measured Bitcoin’s performance on days when a fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 dropped at least 1%.

The report found a similar pattern before US spot Bitcoin ETFs began trading. From 2020 until the January 2024 launch, Bitcoin fell on 74% of the Nasdaq-100 proxy’s large down days, and it fell on 77% from the launch through Nov. 13, 2026.

Yahoo Finance’s adjusted closes show 91 Bitcoin declines across 118 days when QQQ fell at least 1% in the latter period. Bitcoin’s average log return across all 118 days was -1.93%, including days when Bitcoin rose or held steady as well as days when it fell.

QQQ’s return runs from the prior US trading session’s close. Bitcoin’s return runs across consecutive calendar-day closes, with its daily candle ending at midnight UTC, three to four hours after the US stock market closes.

Closing prices alone don't capture the order of moves, and Bitcoin can keep moving for several hours after the US trading session ends, so the comparison includes part of that post-close window.

CryptoSlate compared QQQ and Bitcoin adjusted closes on the same dates using Yahoo Finance data.

Bitcoin closed lower on more than three quarters of the qualifying sessions.

Sessions qualified when QQQ’s daily log return was −1% or lower, regardless of cause. Bitcoin closes at midnight UTC, several hours after U.S. equities.

Use QQQ adjusted-close log returns on U.S. trading days and same-date BTC-USD adjusted-close log returns from Yahoo Finance. Filter at QQQ declines of at least 1%. Divide 91 Bitcoin declines by 118, rounded to 77.1%. The remaining 27 sessions equal 118 minus 91. Bar widths are proportional.

Sessions qualified when QQQ’s daily log return was −1% or lower, regardless of cause. Bitcoin closes at midnight UTC, several hours after U.S. equities.

CME Group research found that Bitcoin and US stocks often moved more closely together in periods of market stress. One possible explanation is the need for cash, since an investor reducing borrowing or covering losses can sell Bitcoin alongside stocks to raise it.

DWF’s results subtracted QQQ’s daily return from Bitcoin’s and SOXX’s returns. On that measure, the two had a correlation of negative 0.30 from March 2026 through the end of the sample. When chip stocks beat the Nasdaq-100 proxy, Bitcoin tended to lag it.

From September 2025 through Nov. 13, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained 85% and Bitcoin fell 39%.

A separate analysis by Block Scholes researcher Thahbib Rahman found that broader market moves explained part of a recent Bitcoin decline. His firm found little evidence that investors sold Bitcoin specifically to buy AI assets.

The Fed held rates in October, and almost all participants judged further increases likely under their baseline outlooks.

US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from September, and the advance estimate showed nominal retail and food services sales up 0.2%, within its margin of error, while industrial production fell 0.4%.

In the Philadelphia Fed’s November manufacturing survey, regional activity fell to 6.3 from 20.9 as the prices-received index rose to 47.0, the highest since June 2022.

Investors should watch whether declines spread across the Nasdaq-100 and how Treasury yields and the Fed rate outlook respond.

A chip-sector drop with little effect on the index would signal Bitcoin differently than a selloff that reaches the rest of the market. Bitcoin’s response would show how closely it is moving with equities in that episode.

"Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

Kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally."

The author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

"With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

In late August, Kiyosaki said on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he said.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

#5248. US Senators Question SEC Tokenized-Stock Exemption Over Wallet Transfers and Investor Protection

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors and prevent illicit transfers. Their November 16 letter, reported by The Block, takes aim at gaps they see in the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for certain trading venues. The development is an oversight challenge, not a court ruling or a notice that the exemption has been cancelled. It goes to a central difficulty for tokenized securities: a regulated purchase can become a blockchain transfer to another address.

The SEC introduced its approach in September, allowing qualifying tokenized-securities venues to operate under a defined exemption from some ordinary exchange-registration requirements. The aim is to permit experimentation with trading stocks in token form while the agency assesses a new market structure. A token representing a security still raises questions about ownership, trading rules and investor rights. The exemptions and their precise conditions matter more than a general statement that securities have moved on-chain. Not every blockchain token, broker or venue automatically qualifies for the same regulatory treatment.

Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto reportedly told SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the framework lacks sufficiently specific safeguards around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering procedures. A buyer verified by a regulated venue might later transfer a token to a wallet whose controller has not undergone the same checks. This problem is not solved merely by verifying the identity of the first purchaser. The letter asks how secondary transfers and the reach of compliance obligations would be managed once tokens circulate beyond the initial venue.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's developing licensing rules.

The senators raised concerns about retail-investor protections and pricing, and reportedly asked whether companies could opt out of having their shares tokenized. Those questions are distinct from financial-crime screening. A token that references equity needs a clear relationship to the rights and obligations of the underlying security, as well as fair information about execution and ownership. If an issuer’s wishes, the investor’s expectations and the platform’s legal structure do not line up, technical transferability alone cannot resolve the conflict. Policymakers must address those issues in enforceable terms.

The lawmakers asked the SEC to explain its approach and urged a transparent rulemaking process for changes in the regulatory treatment of tokenized securities. Such a letter can affect oversight and public debate, especially as control of congressional committees changes, but it is not itself binding legislation. Venues exploring tokenized equities should continue to follow the actual exemption terms and any subsequent SEC guidance. The next concrete milestones are the agency’s response, proposed revisions if any, and how early trading models implement identity, custody and transfer restrictions.

For related context, see our earlier report on new institutional crypto-custody arrangements.

Tokenization can change how securities move, but it does not automatically settle which rules should accompany them. The dispute now concerns the design of that regulatory perimeter, with no basis to describe the senators’ letter as an immediate prohibition on tokenized stocks.

Reporting sources: The Block report of four senators’ letter

The launch combines Android’s global reach with TRON’s leading role in the stablecoin ecosystem, expanding mobile access to onchain savings opportunities that are not accessible on traditional savings apps. Android’s extensive global footprint offers a significant distribution opportunity for digital asset applications, particularly in markets where stablecoins are used for payments, remittances, and savings. Still on-chain data for XRP suggests that despite on-chain indicators looking bullish, the altcoin is struggling to move beyond the $1 psychological level.

Garlinghouse argued that the recent bloodbath across digital assets is less about a fundamental collapse in crypto and more about investors shifting funds to chase the AI boom.

#5242. Bitcoin buyers face a trading issue as stablecoins just suffer their biggest supply drop since 2022

Market makers can advance stablecoins for institutional Bitcoin purchases and settle later against fund holdings, even as marketwide stablecoin supply falls $14.2 billion.

An institutional investor can ask a market maker to buy Bitcoin before the investor has turned tokenized fund shares into cash.

Greg Guttas, head of over-the-counter trading at Flowdesk, told CryptoSlate that the desk could pay with its own stablecoins and settle with the client later against the fund holding.

Securitize and Ethena opened a new route for fund holders on Nov. 12 with a facility for BlackRock’s USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund (BUIDL) that exchanges fund shares for stablecoins outside banking hours. That gives eligible investors a way to raise trading cash themselves.

In Guttas’s example, a dealer would supply the cash for the Bitcoin purchase upfront.

The question of what dealers can spend is sharper after a drop in stablecoin supply. Glassnode reported that aggregate stablecoin supply fell $14.2 billion in the 30 days through Nov. 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022.

The marketwide total leaves open how much an individual desk has on hand and what it would commit to a client’s trade.

Guttas described how an over-the-counter desk could handle a purchase for a client holding tokenized money-market fund shares:

“The market maker in that scenario could use their own stablecoin balances to buy the BTC immediately and then redeem the tokenized MM funds after the fact.”

That sequence would give the client time to settle using the fund position, while the dealer would spend the stablecoins first and wait for settlement to recover them. Until then, those funds would be unavailable for another purchase.

The longer it takes to turn fund shares into settlement cash, the longer the desk has to carry the exposure. Guttas said larger conversions can hit size limits, and weekends can complicate access.

In January 2025, QCP disclosed that it facilitated a six-month Bitcoin basis trade for Securitize Credit using BUIDL as collateral.

A basis trade aims to capture the difference between spot and futures prices, but QCP’s account leaves the funding currency for the Bitcoin leg and the settlement timing undisclosed.

The Securitize and Ethena facility works in both directions for BUIDL. Eligible investors can exchange their fund shares for supported stablecoins, including USDC, or use those stablecoins to acquire BUIDL.

That route can give a fund holder cash to trade on a weekend.

The facility opened with $50 million of inventory, split between $25 million in USDC and $25 million in BUIDL. Securitize said up to another $50 million may become available within about an hour as liquidity is used, subject to terms and availability, bringing the maximum facility capacity to $100 million.

The relevant starting figure for a holder seeking stablecoins at launch was the $25 million in USDC, while the BUIDL side of the inventory serves investors converting stablecoins into fund shares.

Katana CEO Matthew Fisher told CryptoSlate he looks at exchange balances, stablecoins posted as collateral in lending and perpetual futures markets, and how much traders borrow against them.

Those measures help show where stablecoins are being used for trading and leverage, but a balance on an exchange can sit there without becoming a Bitcoin order. Fisher advised watching the deployed number.
